prompt:
A proton enters a uniform magnetic field of flux density $0.25\ \text{T}$ with a speed of $2.0 \times 10^{6}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$, moving perpendicular to the field.

**(a)** Explain why the proton moves in a circle. **[2]**

**(b)** Calculate the radius of the circle. **[2]**

**(c)** Show that the time for one revolution does not depend on the speed of the proton, and calculate it. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** The magnetic force $qvB$ is always perpendicular to the velocity ✓, so it changes the direction but not the speed, and acts as a centripetal force of constant size ✓

**(b)** $qvB = \tfrac{mv^2}{r} \Rightarrow r = \tfrac{mv}{qB}$ ✓ $= \tfrac{1.67 \times 10^{-27} \times 2.0 \times 10^{6}}{1.60 \times 10^{-19} \times 0.25} \approx 0.084\ \text{m}$ ✓

**(c)** $T = \tfrac{2\pi r}{v} = \tfrac{2\pi m}{qB}$, which contains no $v$ ✓; $T = \tfrac{2\pi \times 1.67 \times 10^{-27}}{1.60 \times 10^{-19} \times 0.25} \approx 2.6 \times 10^{-7}\ \text{s}$ ✓
